```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dudkowski_2017_alogliptin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dudkowski_2017_alogliptin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00228-016-2175-1> (open access, PMC5306220)

The final parameter estimates are in the paper's Electronic Supplementary
Material (Supplemental Table 1); the model equations are in the Methods
section "PK/PD modeling and simulations".

# Population

A phase 1, randomized, open-label, single-dose study (NCT00957268) in 46
patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: 9 children (10 to <14 years), 15
adolescents (14 to <18 years) and 22 gender- and race-matched adults (18-65
years). Children and adolescents were randomized 1:1 to a single oral dose of
12.5 or 25 mg alogliptin; all adults received 25 mg. Most subjects were female
(34/46) and Black or African American (32/46). Mean body weight was high in
every arm (86.6-116.3 kg; Table 1), so pediatric and adult weights overlapped
considerably. Most subjects took concomitant metformin. Subjects with renal
impairment (CrCl < 50 mL/min) were excluded.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Dudkowski_2017_alogliptin")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (KA, adults) | log(1.66) 1/h | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `lka_ped` (KA, pediatric) | log(0.590) 1/h | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `lcl` (CL/F, adults) | log(13.0) L/h | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `lcl_ped` (CL/F, pediatric) | log(14.4) L/h | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `lvc` (V2/F) | log(125) L | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `lvp` (V3/F) | log(117) L | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `lq` (Q/F) | log(11.7) L/h | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | 0.75 (fixed) | Methods, PK/PD modeling equation (b = 0.75 for CL/F) |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 1 (fixed) | Methods, PK/PD modeling equation (b = 1 for volume) |
| Reference weight | 70 kg | Methods, PK/PD modeling |
| `e0` | 0 (fixed) | Methods; Supplemental Table 1 |
| `emax` | 99.3 % | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `lec50` (EC50, adults) | log(5.45) ng/mL | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `lec50_ped` (EC50, pediatric) | log(6.38) ng/mL | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `lhill` (shape factor) | log(0.857) | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `etalcl` | 0.185^2 (18.5 %CV) | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `etalvc` | 0.301^2 (30.1 %CV) | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `etalec50` | 0.246^2 (24.6 %CV) | Supplemental Table 1 |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.0820) = 0.286 | Supplemental Table 1 (PK proportional, 28.6 %CV) |
| `addSd` | 0.1 ng/mL (fixed) | Supplemental Table 1 (PK additive variance 0.0100 FIXED) |
| `addSd_Dpp4Inh` | sqrt(3.67) = 1.92 % | Supplemental Table 1 (PD additive) |
| Two-compartment PK, first-order absorption | n/a | Results, PK/PD modeling and simulations |
| `Dpp4Inh = E0 + Emax * Cc^g / (EC50^g + Cc^g)` | n/a | Methods, sigmoid Emax equation |

# Virtual cohorts

Two virtual populations are used.

* **Single-dose study arms.** One cohort of 100 subjects for each of the five
  arms of Table 1, with body weight drawn log-normally around the arm's mean
  weight with the arm's coefficient of variation from Table 1. These are
  compared with the observed non-compartmental results of Tables 2 and 3.
* **Steady-state projection.** As in the paper's simulations, 100 subjects per
  pediatric or adult group, each with body weight drawn from a log-normal
  distribution centred on 95 kg, dosed 12.5 or 25 mg once daily to steady
  state. These are compared with Table 4 and Figure 4.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2017)

obs_sd <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 30, 36, 48, 60, 72)

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~dose, ~CHILD, ~wt_mean, ~wt_sd,
  "Children 12.5 mg", 12.5, 1, 86.62, 13.98,
  "Adolescents 12.5 mg", 12.5, 1, 116.28, 33.16,
  "Children 25 mg", 25, 1, 98.90, 11.96,
  "Adolescents 25 mg", 25, 1, 103.71, 17.10,
  "Adults 25 mg", 25, 0, 92.25, 16.45
)

# The model declares two residual-error endpoints (Cc and Dpp4Inh), so every
# observation row must nominate one through `dvid`; both outputs are returned
# as columns at every observation time whichever is nominated. `addl` repeats
# the once-daily dose (addl = 0 is a single dose).
make_cohort <- function(n, treatment, dose, CHILD, wt_mean, wt_cv, obs_times,
                        id_offset = 0L, addl = 0L) {
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + wt_cv^2))
  subj <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    WT = exp(rnorm(n, log(wt_mean) - sdlog^2 / 2, sdlog)),
    CHILD = CHILD,
    treatment = treatment
  )
  dose_rows <- subj |>
    mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "depot",
           ii = if (addl > 0L) 24 else 0, addl = addl, dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs_rows <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", ii = 0, addl = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, ii, addl, dvid, everything()) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events_sd <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(
    n = 100, treatment = arms$treatment[i], dose = arms$dose[i],
    CHILD = arms$CHILD[i], wt_mean = arms$wt_mean[i],
    wt_cv = arms$wt_sd[i] / arms$wt_mean[i], obs_times = obs_sd,
    id_offset = (i - 1L) * 100L
  )
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_sd[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Single-dose simulation

```{r simulate-sd}
mod <- readModelDb("Dudkowski_2017_alogliptin")
sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_sd, keep = c("treatment", "WT"))
sim_sd <- as.data.frame(sim_sd)
```

```{r figure-1-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figures 1b and 3 of Dudkowski 2017 (mean alogliptin concentration
# and mean DPP-4 inhibition vs time after a single dose), as simulated
# medians with 90% prediction intervals.
sim_sd |>
  select(treatment, time, Cc, Dpp4Inh) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Dpp4Inh), names_to = "output", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(treatment, output, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(value, 0.05), Q50 = median(value), Q95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(output = recode(output, Cc = "Alogliptin (ng/mL)",
                         Dpp4Inh = "DPP-4 inhibition (%)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.1, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~output, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = NULL, colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figures 1 and 3 of Dudkowski 2017.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## PKNCA: alogliptin (Table 2)

```{r pknca-sd}
nca_conc <- sim_sd |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
nca_conc <- bind_rows(
  nca_conc,
  nca_conc |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_df <- events_sd |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published_pk <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "Children 12.5 mg", 57.8, 4.00, 789.3, 16.75,
  "Adolescents 12.5 mg", 44.2, 3.00, 689.0, 15.38,
  "Children 25 mg", 101.4, 2.04, 1222.0, 18.09,
  "Adolescents 25 mg", 96.7, 3.97, 1318.0, 17.15,
  "Adults 25 mg", 136.5, 2.00, 1704.0, 19.33
)

cmp_pk <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_pk,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_pk,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated (median of 100 virtual subjects) vs. observed (Table 2: mean,",
    "median for Tmax) single-dose alogliptin NCA. * differs by >20%."
  )
)
```

The model reproduces `AUC` and half-life within about 16% in every arm and
`Cmax` within 20%. The observed `Cmax` and `AUC` are arithmetic means of 4-22
subjects, whereas the simulated values are medians, so the simulated `Cmax` sits
15-20% below the observed means in every arm. The adolescent 12.5 mg arm has the
highest mean weight (116 kg) and the lowest observed exposure, which the
weight-scaled model also reproduces. The starred `Tmax` rows reflect sampling,
not the model: the study sampled at 1, 2, 4 and 8 h, so observed `Tmax` can only
take those values, while the simulated grid also contains 1.5 and 3 h.

## PKNCA: DPP-4 inhibition (Table 3)

```{r pknca-pd}
nca_pd <- sim_sd |>
  filter(!is.na(Dpp4Inh), time <= 24) |>
  select(id, time, Dpp4Inh, treatment)
nca_pd <- bind_rows(
  nca_pd,
  nca_pd |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Dpp4Inh = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

pd_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_pd, Dpp4Inh ~ time | treatment + id)
pd_intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_pd_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(pd_obj, dose_obj, intervals = pd_intervals))

published_pd <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast,
  "Children 12.5 mg", 83.7, 4.05, 1570,
  "Adolescents 12.5 mg", 81.6, 4.00, 1558,
  "Children 25 mg", 89.3, 2.08, 1699,
  "Adolescents 25 mg", 90.4, 4.00, 1854,
  "Adults 25 mg", 92.7, 2.00, 1890
)

cmp_pd <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_pd_res,
  reference = published_pd,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "%", tmax = "h", auclast = "%*h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
) |>
  mutate(`NCA parameter` = sub("^Cmax", "Emax", `NCA parameter`),
         `NCA parameter` = sub("^Tmax", "Time to Emax", `NCA parameter`),
         `NCA parameter` = sub("^AUClast", "AUEC0-24", `NCA parameter`))
knitr::kable(
  cmp_pd,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated (median) vs. observed (Table 3: mean, median for time to Emax)",
    "DPP-4 inhibition. * differs by >20%."
  )
)

e24 <- sim_sd |>
  filter(time == 24) |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(`Simulated median E24 (%)` = round(median(Dpp4Inh), 1)) |>
  left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~treatment, ~`Observed mean E24 (%)`,
      "Children 12.5 mg", 52.0,
      "Adolescents 12.5 mg", 55.4,
      "Children 25 mg", 57.4,
      "Adolescents 25 mg", 70.4,
      "Adults 25 mg", 72.8
    ),
    by = "treatment"
  )
knitr::kable(e24, caption = "DPP-4 inhibition 24 h after a single dose (Table 3).")
```

The observed time to Emax is the first of the sparse PD samples (2, 4, 8, 12,
24 h) at which the maximum was seen, so it is quantised to 2 or 4 h; the
simulated value comes from a denser grid. Observed `Emax` is also taken over
those sparse samples only. Simulated `Emax` and `AUEC0-24` agree with Table 3
within about 12% in every arm. The 24 h inhibition agrees within about 8% in
every arm except the children's 25 mg arm (4 subjects), where the model
predicts about 68% against an observed mean of 57.4%. That observed value is
well below the adolescents' 70.4% at the same dose despite similar exposure
(Table 2), and the model, which pools children and adolescents, does not
reproduce the difference.

# Steady-state simulation (Table 4 and Figure 4)

```{r cohort-ss}
# Once-daily dosing for 14 days (about 17 terminal half-lives); the last
# dosing interval (312-336 h) is analysed as steady state.
t_ss <- 13 * 24
obs_ss <- t_ss + seq(0, 24, by = 0.5)
ss_groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~dose, ~CHILD,
  "Pediatric 12.5 mg", 12.5, 1,
  "Pediatric 25 mg", 25, 1,
  "Adult 12.5 mg", 12.5, 0,
  "Adult 25 mg", 25, 0
)
events_ss <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ss_groups)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(
    n = 100, treatment = ss_groups$group[i], dose = ss_groups$dose[i],
    CHILD = ss_groups$CHILD[i], wt_mean = 95, wt_cv = 0.20,
    obs_times = obs_ss, id_offset = (i - 1L) * 100L, addl = 13L
  )
}))
sim_ss <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_ss, keep = c("treatment"))) |>
  mutate(time = time - t_ss)
```

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
# Replicates Figure 4 of Dudkowski 2017: steady-state alogliptin concentration
# and DPP-4 inhibition over one 24 h dosing interval (median, 90% PI).
sim_ss |>
  filter(treatment != "Adult 12.5 mg") |>
  select(treatment, time, Cc, Dpp4Inh) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Dpp4Inh), names_to = "output", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(treatment, output, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(value, 0.05), Q50 = median(value), Q95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(output = recode(output, Cc = "Alogliptin (ng/mL)",
                         Dpp4Inh = "DPP-4 inhibition (%)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.3, fill = "red") +
  geom_line(colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_grid(output ~ treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time postdose (h)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Dudkowski 2017.")
```

```{r table-4}
ss_conc <- sim_ss |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
# The last dose of the interval, at the shifted time 0
ss_dose <- events_ss |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
ss_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(ss_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(ss_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))

published_t4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "Pediatric 12.5 mg", 55.6, 729.5,
  "Pediatric 25 mg", 112.2, 1400.2,
  "Adult 12.5 mg", 73.4, 777.2,
  "Adult 25 mg", 147.7, 1575.1
)
cmp_t4 <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = ss_nca,
  reference = published_t4,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_t4, caption = "Steady-state Cmax and AUC0-tau vs. Table 4.")

e24_ss <- sim_ss |>
  filter(time == 24) |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(sim = median(Dpp4Inh)) |>
  left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~treatment, ~pub,
      "Pediatric 12.5 mg", 66.0,
      "Pediatric 25 mg", 75.8,
      "Adult 12.5 mg", 70.5,
      "Adult 25 mg", 79.9
    ),
    by = "treatment"
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - pub) / pub)
e24_ss |>
  mutate(sim = round(sim, 1), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(Group = treatment, `Simulated median E24 (%)` = sim,
         `Table 4 E24 (%)` = pub, `% diff` = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state trough DPP-4 inhibition vs. Table 4.")
```

## Typical-value check against Table 4

The cohort medians above depend on the unpublished spread of the simulated
weights. A deterministic check removes that: the typical subject at 95 kg
(random effects set to zero) must land close to the paper's steady-state
medians, because the paper's cohorts were centred on 95 kg.

```{r typical-check}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
ev_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ss_groups)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(
    n = 1, treatment = ss_groups$group[i], dose = ss_groups$dose[i],
    CHILD = ss_groups$CHILD[i], wt_mean = 95, wt_cv = 0,
    obs_times = t_ss + seq(0, 24, by = 0.05), id_offset = i - 1L, addl = 13L
  )
}))
typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_typ, keep = "treatment")) |>
  mutate(time = time - t_ss)
typ_chk <- typ |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    cmax = max(Cc),
    # dose / CL is the exact steady-state AUC over one dosing interval
    auctau = 1000 * first(ss_groups$dose[match(treatment, ss_groups$group)]) / first(cl),
    e24 = Dpp4Inh[time == 24]
  ) |>
  left_join(published_t4, by = "treatment") |>
  left_join(select(e24_ss, treatment, pub), by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(
    d_cmax = 100 * (cmax.x / cmax.y - 1),
    d_auc = 100 * (auctau / auclast - 1),
    d_e24 = 100 * (e24 / pub - 1)
  )
typ_chk |>
  transmute(
    Group = treatment,
    `Cmax (ng/mL)` = round(cmax.x, 1), `Table 4 Cmax` = cmax.y,
    `AUCtau (ng*h/mL)` = round(auctau, 1), `Table 4 AUCtau` = auclast,
    `E24 (%)` = round(e24, 1), `Table 4 E24` = pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical 95 kg subject at steady state vs. Table 4 medians.")

stopifnot(
  # The typical subject is deterministic, so these hold on any machine. A
  # mis-transcribed CL, V, KA or EC50, or a dropped weight scaling, moves at
  # least one of them by well over 10%.
  all(abs(typ_chk$d_cmax) < 10),
  all(abs(typ_chk$d_auc) < 10),
  all(abs(typ_chk$d_e24) < 10)
)
```

The typical 95 kg subject reproduces Table 4 within about 6% for every group
and metric. The pediatric-vs-adult difference in exposure comes mainly from the
slower pediatric absorption (KA 0.59 vs 1.66 1/h), which lowers Cmax, and the
slightly higher pediatric CL/F, which lowers AUC.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Weight scaling of Q/F and V3/F.** The Methods give the allometric exponents
  only for "CL/F" (0.75) and "Vz/F" (1), while the Results say body weight acts
  on "clearance and volume parameters". The model applies 0.75 to both
  clearances (CL/F, Q/F) and 1 to both volumes (V2/F, V3/F), the usual
  allometric form. Applying the weight effect to CL/F and V2/F only changes the
  Table 4 metrics of a 95 kg subject by less than 1%, so the published
  simulations cannot distinguish the two readings.
- **%CV to variance.** Supplemental Table 1 prints the inter-individual
  variability as %CV. The model uses omega^2 = (%CV/100)^2, the convention the
  same table uses for its proportional residual row (variance 0.0820 printed as
  28.6 %CV). The alternative log(1 + CV^2) differs by under 2%.
- **Shared random effects.** The pediatric and adult rows for CL/F and EC50
  print the same IIV magnitude and %SEM, so one eta each is shared by both age
  groups. KA has no IIV ("NE"); V3/F, Q/F, Emax and the shape factor have IIV
  fixed to 0.
- **Pediatric indicator.** The paper pools children (10 to <14 years) and
  adolescents (14 to <18 years) into one pediatric group in the model; the
  `CHILD` covariate is 1 for both.
- **Residual error.** The PK residual error has a proportional and an additive
  component (additive variance fixed at 0.01, i.e. SD 0.1 ng/mL); the PD
  residual error is additive. The NONMEM coding of the combined error is not
  published; the model uses the sum-of-variances form.
- **Virtual weights.** The paper's simulations drew body weight "from a
  log-normal distribution ... centered around 95 kg" without giving its spread;
  a 20% coefficient of variation was assumed, in line with the arm-level CVs
  of Table 1 (12-29%). The single-dose cohorts use each arm's Table 1 mean and
  SD. Age, sex, race and renal function are not covariates in the final model.
- **Figure 4 caption.** The caption of Figure 4 says "after a single dose", but
  the Results text and the non-zero pre-dose concentrations in the figure show
  that it is the steady state of once-daily dosing; it is replicated here at
  steady state.
- **Errata.** Europe PMC lists no correction or erratum linked to this
  article, and none by the same authors on alogliptin (checked 2026-11-25).
